label: copy-phase input s fed back early (recall 2-3), esp. after c
explanation: Extremely sparse feature (40 activations on dev). About 88% of activations and mass are copy-phase steps where the fed-back input is s, nearly all at recall_idx 2 (the s was original token 1) or 3. The strongest and most common context is a sequence starting c s, so the input pair is c then s (60% of mass), but z s, j s, t p s and c u s also occur. A few scattered activations happen in the original phase on v, 2 or 3. It never fires at the delimiter, at t < 5, or on other copy-phase inputs. Magnitudes are narrow (0.10-0.15) and show no clear modulator. Precision is very low: even c-then-s at recall_idx 2 fires on only about 1% of matching steps, so the feature sits just above threshold and the predicate describes where it can fire, not when it does.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 19 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=s (+2.80), recall_idx=2 & in_tok=s (+2.53), orig0=c (+1.80), orig4=x (+1.69), orig5=v (+1.62), prev_tok=c (+1.53). Lower it: in_count=2 (-1.21), n_digits=2 (-1.17), n_digits=0 (-0.91).
